name: orbit-drawing
purpose: Sizes used only to draw the orbit, optic nerve, and muscles in the binocular stage. None of these affects any computed quantity.
citation: drawing approximation; typical adult proportions pending transcription (orbital rim about 35 mm high and 40 mm wide, orbital depth about 40-45 mm, optic nerve about 3-4 mm in diameter).

orbit.note: Each orbit is drawn as a cone from an elliptical rim, centered on the eye, to the annulus of Zinn at the apex; rimZMm is measured from the globe center (negative is anterior).

opticNerve.note: The nerve leaves the globe about 3 mm nasal to the posterior pole and runs to the annulus.

muscle.note: Tube radii are drawing values; the belly tapers to the tendon over its last tendon length.
muscle.superiorObliqueBelly: The model's superior oblique path starts at the trochlea (its functional origin); the drawing adds the muscle belly from the annulus of Zinn to the trochlea and draws the modeled path as tendon.

targetDrawing.note: Targets farther than maxDrawDistanceMm are drawn at that radius along their direction; the inspector shows the true distance.
